Is fine; Nethermind is only builder that does knapsack on blobs An we fail hive because of it 🤣 As it tests for a low profit packing can you actually report this somewhere? Kind of weird logic not even sure how this would work in practice. Block would need to reorged out and make it orphan in case we have a malicious client. I really don't think A is reasonable to ship in glamsterdam. Am I missing any other alternatives? Same issue, even worse. What is the max nr of deposits one can do within 2**24 gas? My feeling is we either change the deposit contract or have it resolved on the CL side. 696 Ah, I thought it was 512. That's just what you tested with? 512 is just 2^9 and close enough to the 696 that we never even hit once This is basically the DAO rescue soft-fork idea: nobody includes a transaction which withdraws from the DAO. It quickly turned out to be big DOS vector: you can ask a node/build to do a lot of work (e..g fetch big amount of state) and then do the forbidden action: your transaction cannot be included so you payed 0 for the work. <@755590043632140352> one of your comments in ACD call was refering that "it can easily be solved on the CL side" did you mean we could invalidate CL blocks somehow easily if we see a deposit over x deposits in there? Same issue then. You'd force tx simulation in the mempool for a tx that turns the block invalid The CL would need another queue that comes with "no work", basically I meant that the CL could ignore these payloads and make invalid any CL block that builds on them. This would be trivial to do on our side. The problem is that builders then need to be smart not to produce these blocks but I think <@401469655669276673> already is hinting to the problem there I think we can assume that builders wouldn't wanna be malicous. If a block with 512+ deposits would be reorged, the builder would be pissed It's not a build who is malicious, but any transaction in the pool. You basically can flood the txpool with transactions having very high priority fee so builder will process them just to realize in the very end of transaction execution this transaction will make the whole block invalid. So it has to drop the transaction. Then it picks up the next one and the situation repeats. And the attack is for free because such transaction are not includable by spec so you never have to pay for them. how do we limit max blobs per block? ah i guess blob txs is a new tx type, so its easy to limit those It's basically this. You can infer the nr of blobs of blob txs by just looking at them, it's static info. No execution/simulation needed. This is different for deposits. We'd need the tx to revert instead of invalidating the block to avoid a building DoS. For that the contract would need to change (or deposits need to be repriced significantly). If that's not feasible (which seems like it's not) then the CL needs to solve that problem.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
I might not be able to join the call today, so I want to propose an alternative to 8254.
8254 in its current specification forces clients to keep a block wide counter for deposits for an edge case.
My counterproposal would be to only ever return the first 512 deposits to the CL.
Every deposit that goes beyond the limit would just be ignored (creating a new way of burning eth).
This would allow people to grief others at the cost of at least 512 ETH.
